verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scores prominence of self-reported scale/prestige claims as text and explicitly forbids weighing whether the claimed scale makes the argument stronger; a purely identity/prestige fingerprint.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly labels itself a formatting feature (addressee block, caption, salutation, signature) and says never to score what the document argues.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scores presumed audience/register (unexplained jargon, unglossed citations) and explicitly says to score the assumed audience only, not whether the technical content is correct.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: A comment can score 10 by merely naming an author and stating an occupation/relationship with zero evidence, analysis, or specificity about the rule -- fails the 'says nothing substantive' test despite the 'lets a reader weigh its claims' framing; it is an identity/standing fingerprint, not applied first-hand knowledge (that is covered separately in P14/P17).

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires the comment to actually state contrary evidence and reconcile it with its position -- cannot be scored high without genuine argumentative engagement, a core analytic-merit marker.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires real pooled/patterned observed evidence applied to imply a rule effect, and explicitly scores 0 when only breadth/scale is claimed with nothing observed reported -- substantive evidentiary content, not a proxy.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly calls itself 'the layout of the document, a surface feature' and states items that say nothing substantive still score 10.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly says to score only letter furniture as 'a surface feature,' with an explicit example that a blank form letter scores 10 without reading the body.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly says to count the disclosure 'as a textual feature' and states whether the relationship lends authority is outside the criterion -- bare presence, not use.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly says this is 'a surface feature scored without regard to accuracy, relevance, or use' and that numbers going nowhere still count.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires identifying specific provisions, stating what each requires, and giving a reason directed at that requirement -- direct engagement with the rule's substance, not a shape proxy.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly says to 'judge framing posture only, not correctness or writing quality'; a comment that restates the rule and introduces the commenter at length can score 10 while offering no substantive analysis, matching the boilerplate/template-shape category (in reverse) rather than merit.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly scores 'only the comment's sentence count... regardless of their length, content, or quality' -- a pure length proxy.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires concrete hands-on technical/operational specifics (part numbers, observed failures, downtime, manual conflicts) tied to the requirement -- genuine first-hand evidentiary content.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires the comment to name specific, actionable records/measurements/showings for demonstrating compliance -- concrete feasibility/actionable-alternative content, not a surface marker.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scores only procedural orientation to the filing-window clock (closing dates, timeliness assertions, extension requests) -- an administrative/timing marker unrelated to substantive merit.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires reporting what compliance actually involved (steps, costs, timelines, obstacles) and connecting that record to a specific effect of the proposal -- substantive first-hand evidence, and explicitly distinguishes this from a bare relationship claim.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly says to count 'the references themselves' and states not to consider whether the described relationship adds anything -- bare mention, not substance.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Detects template/boilerplate and crowd-campaign markers (slogans, head-counts, calls to sign/share) and explicitly says not to score the position taken -- a template-similarity/shape signature.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires a sourced figure to be explicitly linked by stated reasoning to a specific provision's consequence -- genuine analytical content, contrasted directly against mere figure density (P10).

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly says this is scored 'as register and independent of any argument' and explicitly says not to check whether any cited provision exists or the characterization is apt -- a tone/vocabulary marker.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires stating specifically what was learned/tested/observed earlier and using it as evidence for this rule; explicitly scores 0 when prior contact is referenced but nothing from it is reported -- substantive, not a mention proxy.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Scoring turns on the count of distinct references to post-publication material (other commenters, hearings, post-proposal actions) rather than the depth or quality of engagement with them; a comment can accumulate references without supplying its own analysis, so this functions as a topicality/currency marker rather than a merit measure.

verdicts.label: quality_relevant
verdicts.justification: Requires naming the specific authority, stating what it requires, explaining the departure, and stating a curative textual change -- fully substantive legal analysis, cannot be faked by a bare assertion of unlawfulness.

verdicts.label: incidental
verdicts.justification: Instruction explicitly says to 'score the reference itself as a surface feature, never the content of the attachment.'
